newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cenbank to issue 2,000-crown notes on Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: Czech cenbank to issue 2,000-crown notes on Oct 1.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) said on Wednesday it would begin putting a new 2,000 crown bill into circulation from October 1.
In a statement, the central bank said that the reason for adding the new note was to reduce the costs on paper money in circulation.
It said that 1,000 crown notes currently make up about 55 percent of the value of money in circulation, while 5,000 crown notes comprised about 25 percent.

"The CNB expects that after issuance of the banknotes in the nominal value of 2,000 crowns the amount of 1,000 crown denominated bank notes in circulation will significantly drop," the statement said.
The 1,000 crown notes currently comprise about 30 percent. of the total number of 24 million banknotes in circulation.

The musically-themed 2,000 crown banknotes will feature a portrait of the late Czech opera singer Ema Destinnova and will have various high-tech security features built into each bill to prevent forgeries.
